newsitem.title: USA: Interra adopts rights plan, files shelf.
newsitem.headline: Interra adopts rights plan, files shelf.

text.p: Interra Financial Inc said Wednesday its directors adopted a shareholder rights plan to protect the long-term interests of the company's shareholders, and approved a plan to sell up to $200 million in debt or equity securities at its discretion.

Interra, parent of Minneapolis-based Dain Bosworth and Dallas-based Rauscher Pierce Refsnes, adopted a 10-year stockholder rights plan that gives each shareholder the right to purchase a newly authorized series of preferred stock, in the event that a tender offer for the company is announced, or an acquirer purchases at least 15 percent of the common stock.
"A shareholder rights plan encourages any prospective buyer to negotiate with our board," said Irving Weiser, chairman and chief executive of Interra, in a statement.

After any acquirer purchases at least 15 percent of the outstanding common stock, Interra shareholders other than the acquirer could then purchase Interra common stock at a 50-percent discount from market price, rendering any hostile takeover prohibitively expensive for a would-be acquirer.

"Although we would be surprised if any prospective buyer chose to acquire a brokerage firm without negotiating with the board, we have decided to add this measure to protect against those who may not understand our industry," Weiser said.
The new purchase rights will attach to all Interra common shares outstanding at the close of business on May 12, 1997.

In other action, Interra said its board approved the filing of a universal shelf registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. It would permit Interra to sell at its discretion up to $200 million in secured or unsecured debt, or equity securities. Interra said it intends to file the shelf registration statement in May. Interra
said it may use proceeds to finance acquisitions, subsidiary financing, or other corporate purposes. Interra said it has no current plans to issue any shelf securities.
"We are laying the foundation for continued growth of the company," Weiser said.
